summary: On 7 January 2019 a retry storm from one application overloaded CoreDNS in Zalando's Kubernetes clusters. Pods were killed for running out of memory, DNS went down and product pages failed for over an hour.

overview.background: Zalando runs Kubernetes on AWS. Applications resolve names through CoreDNS pods in the cluster. Monitoring also ran inside the cluster.
systems: Aggregation layer for product and outfit pages
overview.impact: Product and outfit pages returned errors for over one hour.
overview.severity: Customer-facing outage. The postmortem is published in Zalando's Kubernetes documentation.
overview.gaps: The postmortem gives no clock times, so none are shown.

archNote: Components and the chain of events are from the postmortem. The layout is ours.

diagrams.title: A retry storm exhausts DNS
diagrams.caption: Timeouts to a non-critical service caused 404s and client retries. More traffic meant more DNS queries, and CoreDNS ran out of memory.

nodes.label: Node.js apps: no DNS cache, ndots 5

diagrams.title: Cached DNS and outside monitoring (conceptual)
diagrams.caption: Zalando raised CoreDNS memory, planned dnsmasq on every node and external alerting. This picture shows the shape of those fixes.

afterChanges: Most lookups are served from a cache on the same node.
Alerts do not depend on the cluster they watch.
afterNote: One application should not be able to take out DNS, and the fixes enforce that.
timelineNote: The postmortem describes the sequence without clock times.

timeline.e: Timeouts to a non-critical downstream service make the aggregation layer return 404s, and clients retry.
Ingress traffic and DNS queries spike.
CoreDNS pods are killed for running out of memory and DNS is fully down.
Circuit breakers open. In-cluster monitoring is down with DNS, so on-call staff are reached manually.
CoreDNS memory is raised from 100Mi to 2000Mi.
Product and outfit pages work again.

rootCause.trigger: Timeouts to a non-critical service caused 404s and client retries, sharply raising traffic.
rootCause.underlying: CoreDNS pods had a 100Mi memory limit that could not handle the query volume and were killed repeatedly.
contributing: Node.js default DNS has no caching
ndots 5 turns one external lookup into about 10 queries
Short connection lifetimes cause many lookups
No vertical pod autoscaler for CoreDNS
Monitoring ran inside the same cluster
propagation: Every service in the cluster loses name resolution.

evidence.label: The key finding
evidence.body: It should not be possible for a single application to “DoS” our DNS infrastructure.

evidence.label: Simulated DNS check
evidence.body:
$ kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=kube-dns
NAME            READY  STATUS     RESTARTS
coredns-abc12   0/1    OOMKilled  14
$ kubectl -n kube-system top pod -l k8s-app=kube-dns
evidence.note: Output invented to show the symptom.

evidence.label: Simulated resolver setting
evidence.note: A pod-level setting that reduces query multiplication. Teaching example.

diagnose.step: Check CoreDNS pod status and restarts.
diagnose.why: OOM kills explain total DNS loss.

diagnose.step: Look at the reason for the last restart.
diagnose.cmd: kubectl -n kube-system describe pod -l k8s-app=kube-dns | grep -A3 'Last State'

diagnose.step: Find what generates the query load.

correct.step: Reduce the retry storm at the source.
correct.why: Circuit breakers and backoff reduce amplification.

verify.step: Resolve a name from a test pod.

verify.why: Stable pods show the limit is adequate.

prevent.step: Run a DNS cache on every node.
prevent.why: Zalando planned dnsmasq in front of CoreDNS.

prevent.step: Lower ndots or use fully qualified names for external hosts.

fix.safety: Raising memory limits may need node capacity and can hide a retry storm. Fix amplification too. Edit resources in a controlled change.

troubleshoot.scenario: Everything in the cluster fails to resolve names. Dashboards are blank. CoreDNS pods keep restarting.
clues: Traffic spiked after a downstream timeout
troubleshoot.question: What do you do to restore service and why did the spike happen?
troubleshoot.answer: Raise the CoreDNS memory limit to stop the restarts, use a test pod to confirm resolution, then trace the retry storm and reduce DNS amplification with caching and lower ndots.

options: CoreDNS pods ran out of memory under a surge of queries
rootcause.why: The postmortem states pods were OOM killed.

remediation.answer: With ndots 5, a name with fewer than five dots is tried with each search domain first, so one external name can produce around 10 queries.
Run a probe from outside the cluster against an ingress and DNS, and page from an external service.
Set requests and limits based on peak tests, add autoscaling, and alert on restarts and query rate.

design.prompt: Design DNS so that one misbehaving app cannot affect others.
constraints: Must stay up if CoreDNS dies
design.answer: Use node-local caches, rate limit per source, set sensible ndots, autoscale CoreDNS, keep cached answers when upstream is down, and monitor externally.

checks.q: What was CoreDNS memory raised from and to?

options: It ran inside the cluster and depended on DNS
checks.why: The postmortem says monitoring went down with DNS.

checks.q: What fix did Zalando plan on each node?
checks.why: They planned dnsmasq on every node.

monitoring: Alert on CoreDNS restarts and query rates
practices: Retry with backoff and circuit breakers
Make escalation easy when tools are down
